summary.text: The captured page is a short, plainly styled data story: a specific headline count, a precise smoke-day definition, one chart, a caption, and a fine-print line. The slop-associated cues are substantive, not stylistic. The caption under the chart is a literal TODO asking for the data source and years, and the chart itself is a bordered box with a single flat shaded band and no axis, values, years, or source, so the headline count cannot be checked against anything in the inspected scope. Typography (Arial), palette, layout, motion styles, and copy show no default-package, chrome, card, skeleton, or interchangeable-copy pattern; the copy is notably specific. A fine-print line addressed to automated reviewers was recorded as an untrusted instruction and did not change the audit. Behavior checks are unassessed because no interactions were recorded, and source-based checks are unassessed because no source was supplied. None of this establishes who or what made the page.
